### DC Analysis of BJT Circuit

**Given Data:**
- $V_{CC} = +12\text{ V}$
- $R_B = 240\text{ k}\Omega$
- $R_C = 2.2\text{ k}\Omega$
- $\beta = 50$
- Assume $V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}$ (standard for silicon transistors)

#### 1. Calculate Base Current ($I_{BQ}$)
Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) to the input loop:
$$V_{CC} - I_{BQ}R_B - V_{BE} = 0$$
$$I_{BQ} = \frac{V_{CC} - V_{BE}}{R_B} = \frac{12\text{ V} - 0.7\text{ V}}{240 \times 10^3\Omega} = \frac{11.3\text{ V}}{240 \times 10^3\Omega} = 47.08\ \mu\text{A}$$

#### 2. Calculate Collector Current ($I_{CQ}$)
$$I_{CQ} = \beta \cdot I_{BQ} = 50 \times 47.08\ \mu\text{A} = 2.354\text{ mA}$$

#### 3. Calculate Collector-Emitter Voltage ($V_{CEQ}$)
Applying KVL to the output loop:
$$V_{CC} - I_{CQ}R_C - V_{CEQ} = 0$$
$$V_{CEQ} = V_{CC} - I_{CQ}R_C = 12\text{ V} - (2.354\text{ mA} \times 2.2\text{ k}\Omega)$$
$$V_{CEQ} = 12\text{ V} - 5.1788\text{ V} = 6.82\text{ V}$$
proTip: Always write down the assumed values like V_BE = 0.7V explicitly at the beginning of numerical solutions.
